method: A table procedure with two word lists and one rule about the line, fitted on public paragraph text only. List one holds the words that stand first in a line on the public pages, list two the words that stand anywhere else. Every line has nine words: the first is drawn by frequency from list one, the other eight by frequency from list two. Words are independent draws: no word order, no meaning. 2,600 lines, fixed seed, generated once, laid on the pages line by line (cut lines). The writer sees where a line starts and nothing else. On the practice split the line-initial mean length is 4.90 glyphs against the manuscript's 4.83, above the within-line shuffle. So F-006 needs a writer who treats the start of a line differently, not a language.
